check.flow.endsOutside: {start}, which branches off from {name}, ends without reaching a join (connect each branch to a node of kind: join)
check.flow.noBegin: There is no begin node (kind: begin). Put one in the flow
check.flow.noJoin: The branches from {name} do not reach a join (merge them at a node of kind: join)
check.flow.noPartner: {name}: who begin {node} receives from is not written (draw partner lines or write program, or write anyCaller: true if any caller may call it)
check.flow.otherJoins: The branches from {name} reach different joins ({joins}) (merge them at the same join node)
check.flow.selfLoop: {name}: the next of node {nodes} goes back to itself (there is no way out. To repeat, put an eval node in between and write where to exit to)
check.flow.unlinkedPartner: {name}: the partner {program} of {place} is text but has the name of {names} (draw it as a partner line)
check.flow.unreachable: {name}: nothing leads to node {nodes} (it cannot be reached from the begin node by following the exits. Connect it from some node with a next, branch or else line, or delete it)
check.flow.whyBranch: (a fork. Write the condition as text in the field when)
check.flow.whyElse: (where to go when no branch matches. Required)
check.flow.whyEventBegin: (trigger: event needs an awaits line to the flow it waits for, and its result in the field outcome)
check.flow.whyEventWait: (for: event needs an awaits line to the flow it waits for, and the field outcome)
check.flow.whyJoin: (all: when all have arrived, any: when any one has, first: when the first one has, cancelling the others)
check.flow.whySteps: (list reading, writing, signing, verifying, calling, sending, receiving and computing as rows)
check.frame.gone: The section it points at is not there (removed, or not in this tree)
check.frame.notUi: What it points at, {path}, is not a ui section
check.ghost.noCard: What it points at, {target}, does not lead to a card
check.ghost.none: It points at nothing (the card it pointed at was deleted. Re-attach it with card_update's target, or delete it with card_delete)
check.ghost.round: Following what it points at goes in a circle (re-attach it with card_update's target)
check.id.control: {field} cannot have a line break, a tab or another control character
check.line.noFile: The file is not there (it is not made yet, or it was deleted or moved. If you made it, re-read the working directory. If it moved, re-attach it with card_update's connections)
check.line.noPartner: The partner card is not there (it was deleted. Re-attach it with card_update's connections, or remove the line)
check.line.noRow: {name} has {rows} process rows ({from} does not exist)
check.line.noShape: The shape card is not there (it was deleted. Re-attach it with card_update's of)
check.line.noSymbol: There is no {symbol} in {file} (nearest: {near}. If it was renamed, draw the line again to the name it has now with card_update's connections)
check.node.anyCallerAlone: anyCaller of {name} (begin) cannot be written together with partners (partner lines, program); choose one
check.node.dupNext: {name} has two next lines to the same destination
check.node.duplicate: There are two nodes named {name} (a name is used once within a flow)
check.node.emptyWhen: The when of condition line {n} of {name} is empty (write the condition as text)
check.node.kindIs: The kind of {name} must be one of {kinds} (not {kind})
check.node.manyBegins: There are {count} begin nodes ({names}). Keep only one
check.node.noTarget: {name} leads to {to}, but there is no such node (the nodes are {names})
check.node.noTargets: {name}: targets is not used. For parallel paths, make the previous node's next an array (["a", "b"]) to split, and merge them at a node of kind: join (see about: flow in guide)
check.node.receiveOnly: {stray} of {name} (begin) can be written only with trigger: receive
check.node.timeoutPair: The onTimeout line of {name} is written together with the field timeout
check.path.noNames: Nothing inside {at} can be pointed at by name (it has no shape, or it is inside a list with no element picked)
check.path.notItemRow: {at} is a row that is not an item, so nothing inside it can be pointed at
check.path.notWriting: {path} is not a note, freedoc or formatdoc (or an item of one)
check.path.onlyItems: {path}: to point inside, point at an item of a formatdoc
check.path.sectionColon: Write a section with a colon: "[[{path}:]]"
check.peer.noReceiverReturn: Nothing in {there} takes from {name} (a begin with trigger receive, a receive row, or a run that runs {name}. Draw a partner line to {name}, leave the partner unwritten, or draw the run's runs line to {name}). If this does not return to {there}, remove the partner line from here to {there}
check.peer.noReceiverSend: Nothing in {there} takes from {name} (a begin with trigger receive, or a receive row. Draw a partner line to {name}, or leave the partner unwritten). If this does not send to {there}, remove the partner line from here to {there}
check.peer.noSenderReceive: Nothing in {there} sends to {name} (a send row, the return of an end, or a run that runs {name}. Draw a partner line to {name}, or draw the run's runs line to {name}). If this does not receive from {there}, remove the partner line from here to {there}
check.peer.noSenderWait: Nothing in {there} sends to {name} (a send row or the return of an end. Draw a partner line to {name}, or call {there} from {name} with send, call or run and leave the partner of the return unwritten). If this does not receive from {there}, remove the partner line from here to {there}
check.peer.notReturned: Of what is received ({carries}), no end of {there} returns {missing}: {others}
check.peer.notSent: Of what is received ({carries}), no sender sends {missing}: {others}
check.peer.receivesMismatch: What is received ({carries}) does not match what is sent from {there}: {others}
check.peer.returnsNotReceived: What is received ({carries}) does not take {missing}, which an end of {there} returns (a receive row waiting for the answer to a call takes what every end that may return carries): {others}
check.peer.sendsMismatch: What is sent ({carries}) does not match what the receiver in {there} takes: {others}
check.peer.sendsNotReceived: What is received ({carries}) does not take {missing}, which {there} sends: {others}
check.peer.sendsNotTaken: Of what is sent ({carries}), the receiver in {there} does not take {missing}: {others}
check.rows.callFlow: {here} (call): calling another flow and waiting for it to finish is done by a run node (kind: run and the runs line). A call row is for a program that is not in the project (program)
check.rows.callNeedsProgram: {here} (call) needs program (the program to call). Calling another flow and waiting for it to finish is done by a run node (kind: run and the runs line)
check.rows.needsKey: {here} ({op}) needs a key line (from: {here}, fields.use: {op}; the key)
check.rows.noGroup: {here}: a process node's rows cannot have {op}. Forks and loops are written with an eval node (kind: eval), and parallel paths with two or more next lines and a join (kind: join)
check.rows.noReturn: {here}: a process node's rows cannot have return. Returning is done by the return of an end node (kind: end)
check.rows.sendNeedsPartner: {here} (send) needs a partner: partner lines (from: {here}; the partner flows; any number) or program (a program that is not in the project)
check.rows.strayNone: {here} ({op}) cannot have {stray}. A {op} row says what it does in its description
check.rows.tooMany: steps can have at most 300 rows in all
